subject: Order Form: invoice allocation & VAT responsibility
body:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — invoicing & VAT questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is ready to move forward but we need to resolve two quick commercial items before Legal will sign the Order Form:

1) VAT handling: Acme has EU entities in DE and FR. Our finance team wants to confirm whether Redwood will invoice Acme NV (EU entity) and treat VAT as reverse charge, or whether Redwood requests invoices to the US entity and Acme will self-account.

2) Invoice splitting and PO flow: we need invoices split by legal entity (DE / FR) for local AP and tax reclaim. Can you confirm Redwood can emit multiple invoices from the same Order Form, or whether we should set up separate order forms per entity?

Also, our standard net terms are net-45. Your order form lists net-30; would Redwood accept net-45 for this deal?

Appreciate a quick runbook so we can loop Legal/Tax and wrap up.

Best,
Jane Doe
Head of Procurement — Acme Corp
Jane.Doe@acme.com

---
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — invoicing & VAT questions

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Finance/Sales Ops) to confirm approach and next steps. High level:

- We can support splitting invoices by legal entity if you provide the billing contacts and PO numbers for each entity. That typically requires an invoice matrix on our side.
- VAT: Redwood's standard is to invoice the contracting entity on the Order Form. For EU reverse-charge, we can indicate VAT = 0 on invoice if you provide VAT IDs and the appropriate EU registration details; otherwise VAT will be applied per local rules.
- Net terms: I can escalate net-45 to my manager; need internal approval for this deal.

Laura/Karthik — can you confirm what we need from Acme to produce separate invoices and whether net-45 is approvable for a first-year ARR level of $420k (ACV)?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0112

---
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — invoicing & VAT questions

Thanks Rishi — looping Legal & Tax. Jane — quick answers and recommended redlines attached. See attached PDF (ACME_Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) for tracked changes; synopsis below: 

1) Invoicing by entity: We can issue multiple invoices referencing the same Order Form provided each invoice lists the purchasing legal entity, its PO, and billing address. We will need an invoice_matrix.xlsx (sample attached) populated with: entity name, billing address, VAT/Tax ID, AP contact, PO number, and currency.

2) VAT treatment: If Acme provides valid EU VAT IDs and the contracting party on the Order Form is an EU entity, we will apply reverse-charge (VAT = 0) and include the reverse-charge note on the invoice. If the contracting party is the US entity, Redwood must charge VAT where applicable and Acme may need to reclaim locally. Our redline clarifies that VAT responsibilities follow the contracting entity and lists required documentation.

3) Net terms: Standard is net-30; I can approve net-45 only with finance sign-off and a credit review. Karthik, can you run the credit/AR risk and advise if net-45 is acceptable for this ACV and whether we require a deposit/advance?

4) Tax residency / local invoicing: If you need invoices issued from Redwood EU legal entity (for local tax purposes), we need to confirm Redwood's EU taxable presence and ensure the Order Form references the EU billing entity. That is more involved and may require separate Order Forms per legal entity.

Please review the attached redline and populate the invoice matrix. Once we have the populated matrix I can prepare the final Order Form for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: ACME_Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline of Order Form; summary above)
Attachment: invoice_matrix.xlsx (sample template to populate entity/PO info)

---
On Wed, 29 Jul 2026 at 10:47 AM, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com> wrote:
> Hi Laura / Rishi,
>
> Thanks — we'll fill out invoice_matrix.xlsx and confirm entity VAT IDs. Quick question: for operational simplicity our tax team prefers a single invoice from Redwood US (Acme will re-allocate internally). Would Redwood be able to include reversal language for VAT reclaim if we provide VAT IDs later?
>
> Also, regarding net terms: our AP team is firm on net-45 for new vendors. If Redwood needs a short deposit instead, tell us the amount and we can consider.
>
> Best,
> Tom
> Procurement Operations — Acme Corp
>
---
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — invoicing & VAT questions

Hi all,

Quick finance notes:
- Net-45: For this deal size (ACV ~$420k) we can approve net-45 if Acme signs a standard credit application and we obtain a one-month advance (approx. 1/12 of ARR) to mitigate AR risk. If Acme prefers no advance, escalation to Revenue Ops is required and approval may take 3–4 business days.
- Invoice splitting: We can generate multiple invoices under one Order Form. However, our billing system requires the invoice_matrix with exact entity legal names and VAT IDs before we can schedule invoice delivery.
- Tax invoices from Redwood EU: That's feasible but requires contracting with the Redwood EU invoicing entity; we'd need a separate Order Form or explicit billing entity clause. That typically delays lead time by 7–10 business days.

I've attached a blank invoice matrix (invoice_matrix.xlsx). Rishi / Marissa — I'll coordinate the credit check and send a short Credit App link to Acme if they accept net-45 + 1-month advance.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: invoice_matrix.xlsx

---
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — invoicing & VAT questions

Thanks everyone — we populated invoice_matrix.xlsx with two rows (Acme DE and Acme FR) and included VAT IDs and PO numbers. We prefer not to do an advance if possible. If an advance is required to get net-45, please propose an amount and we'll take it to leadership.

I uploaded the completed matrix here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-orderform-v3 (same link as above).

Jane

---
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — invoicing & VAT questions

Great — thanks for the matrix, Jane. Per Karthik: we can accept net-45 subject to a short one-month advance OR escalation (which will add time). I've proposed a compromise to Sales Leadership and approved internally: Redwood will accept net-45 with no advance if Acme signs the attached revenue assurance addendum. Laura has added the clause to the redline.

Next steps: 
1) Laura — final redline attached (ACME_Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf).
2) Acme — please confirm you accept the revenue assurance addendum and we will push the Order Form to DocuSign.
3) Marissa/Karthik — once signed, billing will generate split invoices per the uploaded invoice_matrix.

DocuSign link (live once Acme confirms): https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abcdef123456

If all good, I'll send the DocuSign envelope and include the PO numbers so your AP team has a one-click receipt.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you live.

Rishi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
